title: ÆTHER: Neon Raja v2 (handpan)
maker: ElevenLabs Music API on the owner's paid plan

positive_global_styles: a regal, dark cyberpunk king's theme for a film score: slow-burning 1980s synthwave with a master handpan player as the featured solo voice, mysterious and majestic, composed and played like a senior blockbuster film composer with a virtuoso soloist
C sharp minor with a raised seventh, like raga Kiravani, about 103 BPM, a slow dark build

about half real instruments (a handpan played expressively with ghost notes, fingertip rolls, harmonics and slaps; a talkbox nadaswaram; thavil; strings; low brass) and half fresh electronics (deep wide sub bass, analog synth arpeggios, warm retro synth lead, gated 80s drums), each clearly heard

the handpan is the soul of the track: it plays the melody with human timing, breath-like pauses, small grace notes and dynamics; the talkbox nadaswaram and glitch-chopped veena answer it; a pitched-down mridangam is the deep bass hit
the neon city's own sounds as instruments: neon-tube buzz as the pad, servo whirs as fills, a hologram-crown chime as the bell, a metal throne clank as the snare, rain on neon signs as the hi-hat
a singable melody of question-and-answer phrases with a catchy 5-note riff that varies slightly on each repeat, a moving bass line, a string counter-melody, space between phrases
dark, warm, wide, glossy mix with a very deep sub, the handpan close and intimate in front

positive_local_styles: the first sound at second zero: one deep handpan note with a low mridangam boom under it, then neon-tube buzz and rain
the handpan alone, rubato, plays a rising 3-note call (root, minor third, fifth), the last note ringing with a soft harmonic; a small grace note before the second phrase
transition: the handpan plays a short pickup phrase into the next bar; a very deep wide sub bass and a slow analog synth arpeggio join one at a time
the handpan's ghost-note taps become a soft pulse, the talkbox nadaswaram answers its phrase once; nuance: one fingertip roll on the last beat
transition: the strings enter with a held low note under the handpan, which states the catchy 5-note riff
tension grows slowly, servo whirs and the neon buzz rise in the background; nuance: the handpan slows the last note of a phrase like a breath, then answers itself
transition: one reversed veena swell into a massive hit, the main reveal: gated drums, bold low brass and the synth lead carry the riff, a deep wordless male choir
the handpan plays the riff over the full band with slaps on the accents, the nadaswaram answers with gamakam slides; nuance: the riff's last note changes once to a borrowed chord
the band drops to the deep sub and a soft drum pulse; a virtuoso handpan solo with fast rolls, harmonics and slaps, playful and masterly, like an interlude showpiece in a hit film song
the strings and synth lead answer its last phrase and the full band returns bigger
the riff played biggest by the whole band with the choir, then one final unison hit with a deep sub boom
only neon-tube buzz and rain remain, and the handpan alone plays the rising 3-note call one last time, the last note ringing out

brief.notes: Jithesh 29 Oct 16:49 on v1: picked take 2, 'but need minute nuances and touch of a senior musician with one instrument like a handpan or aerophone'. v2 keeps take 2's character (slow dark burn, deep wide sub, drums only from ~28 s, C# minor, 103 BPM) and adds ONE featured solo voice: a handpan played by a master, rubato and expressive (ghost notes, fingertip rolls, harmonics, slaps, space between phrases). Minute nuances: each section gets one different small played detail, used once. Rules: music-scoring.md section 9 (motif at start and end, one reversed veena swell at the reveal, composed transitions, rule 14 senior craft).

story: A king rules a rain-soaked neon city of the future. The city's power fails, he wakes it again, and it crowns him.
human_work: to be added by the owner: melody, take choice, edits, mix
